research_question: What material redesign could make a natural-gas volatility experiment detect the frozen 5% QLIKE MEPI without reusing protected outcomes?
search_scope: Pre-feasibility refresh of peer-reviewed HAR/realized-volatility and natural-gas event-volatility literature. Claims are used to define mechanisms and nuisance-only redesign classes; no protected Commodity volatility outcomes were inspected.

sources.title: A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility
Weather, storage, and natural gas price dynamics: Fundamentals and volatility
Natural gas prices and the gas storage report: Public news and volatility in energy futures markets
Exploiting dependence: Day-ahead volatility forecasting for crude oil and natural gas exchange-traded funds

claim_map.claim: HAR-type realized-volatility models are a parsimonious way to represent persistent multi-horizon volatility components, so the positive HAR diagnostic has a plausible prior mechanism but is not itself confirmation.

Natural-gas volatility responds to fundamental information including weather and storage-report timing, so mechanism-specific event conditioning is scientifically distinct from an arbitrary horizon sweep.
Adding related-market or model complexity does not reliably improve natural-gas volatility forecasts, so model expansion alone is not a material reopening condition.

expected_observations: A credible reopening should add genuinely independent information or isolate a mechanism-specific event population rather than merely re-aggregate the same calendar outcomes.

Persistence can make HAR-style forecasting plausible while simultaneously reducing effective independent information, so nuisance-only dependence sensitivities must clear the MEPI before confirmation.

Event conditioning tied to ex-ante fundamental information can be scientifically distinct, but it must lower nuisance variance or increase independent event count enough to clear the frozen 5% QLIKE MEPI.
disconfirming_observations: The same daily design requires an implausibly large history under the already observed nuisance scale to detect a 5% QLIKE improvement across all dependence sensitivities.
The non-overlapping five-session event redesign still requires thousands of independent events under its observed nuisance scale.
A proposed successor differs only by horizon, model complexity, relabeling calendar rows, or reuse of consumed outcomes rather than by mechanism or independent-information structure.
No fresh confirmation path remains after accounting for the consumed diagnostic lineage and prior adaptive design choices.
